inlines.v: OB'LOQUY, noun [Latin obloquor; ob and loquor, to speak.] 1. Censorious speech; reproachful language; language that casts contempt on men or their actions. Shall names that made your city the glory of the earth, be mentioned with obloquy and detraction? 2. Cause of reproach; disgrace. [Not used.]
